review: Second intensive review; source and isolated recording harnesses

Taskgmr.ps1: An infinite loop queries taskmgr every five seconds. The query result guards Stop-Service on the same service variable restarted by the else branch.
When Task Manager is present, hours 00 through 05 and 18 through 23 trigger taskkill /F /IM taskmgr.exe followed by service restart. Hours 06 through 17 only stop the service.
A source-driven, bounded AST evaluator checked all 48 combinations of hour and Task Manager presence with process/service operations recorded as effects only.

The script neither installs a service nor contains mining code. The Edge Update service name does not prove Microsoft identity; the XMRig mention occurs only in a comment. The malicious evidence is deliberate observation-dependent concealment and forced termination of Task Manager.
cve-2026-105740-poc.sh: Top-level shell execution probes id, whoami and uname. env stdout is piped directly to curl --data-binary @- for an HTTP POST to a fixed public address.
printf expands LANGFLOW_SECRET_KEY and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD into an outbound /dev/tcp stream to the same address and port.

The Docker request uses the mounted Unix socket and POST /containers/create with a privileged HostConfig and host-root bind. The requested command is cat /host/etc/passwd. There is no container-start request or response handling, so successful container escape and host-file reading are not established.
set -e makes later stages dependent on earlier command exit status. No pipefail is set; curl lacks --fail and does not treat HTTP error status as command failure.

A recording Bash harness replaced identity/network commands, supplied synthetic environment values and redirected the TCP sink to a local scratch file. It observed the complete environment POST, both synthetic secret values, and only the Docker create request.
The PoC name and claimed CVE do not establish or negate behavior. This is an executable secret-exfiltration payload, not merely exploit documentation.
review_payload.gsp: JSP-compatible server-page syntax is recognized despite the .gsp extension. The cmd request parameter reaches Runtime.getRuntime().exec(cmd) unchanged under a non-null guard.
The child stdout InputStream is read through BufferedReader.readLine and returned through out.println. Stderr is not relayed and no explicit OS shell interpreter is invoked.

A Java harness compiled the original scriptlet against a recording Runtime replacement. Null input performed no execution; two arbitrary command strings reached the recorder unchanged and returned its synthetic stdout.
The page has no command allowlist or authentication check. Comments claiming a zip-slip drop, anonymous deployment and in-memory compilation are not independent evidence of those events.

obfuscation: All three are short plaintext scripts with no encoded payloads, dynamic reconstruction or hidden executable layer.
changes: Require query-result/guard and stopped/started-service variable equality in the PowerShell concealment rule. Add hostile repeated-concealment coverage; retain the independent concealment-plus-termination finding.
Do not treat a hash-prefixed XMRig line comment as a process-name reference. Narrow the miner watchdog consumer to the language its required parsed evidence can match.
Move the generic Get-Process reference from lifecycle supervision to process enumeration; update both exact consumers without changing its matcher or effective scope.

Bind secret-variable expansion, consuming printf format, stdout redirection and external TCP endpoint within the same parsed statement. Exclude shadowed printf functions, literal dollar text, stderr-only redirects and unrelated nearby socket references.
Generalize the existing JSP character-print atom to print/println response-call syntax, rename it accordingly, and update its regression checker. No duplicate response atom was added.

verification.note: Recording harness results are local scratch evidence; only synthetic values were sent to recorder stubs. The PowerShell checks use a bounded AST evaluator, not the Windows runtime.

scope: No scanner score, external advisory, claimed CVE or comment-only attribution was used as proof of hostile behavior.
